title: Karuna Nidhi Tiwari v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd.
coram: Arun Tandon, J. and Harsh Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner relegated to higher authority under 4.6(f).
headnote: A grievance as to the total money demanded for providing an electricity connection is to be examined by the authority one step higher than the officer who made the impugned order, under clause 4.6(f) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was disposed of with liberty to approach that authority, which is to decide the representation in accordance with law by a reasoned speaking order.
facts: Karuna Nidhi Tiwari approached the Allahabad High Court in a writ petition against U.P. Power Corporation Ltd., through its Managing Director, and three others. His grievance was the total sum demanded as a condition of providing an electricity connection to his installation. The petitioner was represented by Mahboob Ahmad; the standing counsel appeared for the State respondents. The Court heard both sides on that limited complaint and did not inquire into how the demand had been computed.

holding_units.holding: Issues as to the total money demanded for providing an electricity connection can be examined by the authority one step higher than the authority who made the impugned order, under clause 4.6(f) of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner was permitted to approach that higher authority within two weeks; on such representation the higher authority shall consider and decide the same in accordance with law by a reasoned speaking order, preferably within eight weeks.

not_decided.point: Whether the quantum of money demanded for the connection was lawful
not_decided.note: Left to the next higher authority under clause 4.6(f).
